identity.description:
Add the orchestrator record, its command line, and the project lead's reports

## Summary

An orchestrator session that runs many project leads now has a durable record of its own, and one command that is the only writer of it. The record holds the items and their stages, groups of related items with their merge order, one inbox for the principal (decisions, questions, ideas and notices that stay until they are answered or dismissed), the plan with each change and its reason, and a copy of what each implementer was told. The same command reads PR, check, review and merge-queue state from GitHub and prints the agreed board as text. A project lead that an orchestrator started reports its stage and records its questions there; a run with no orchestrator is unchanged.

Closes #151

**Ticket:** https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/151 (part 1 of https://github.com/jerridan/crew/issues/150)
**Type:** New feature

---

## Agent context

### Authority

- Issue 150 (the agreed design: rules 9, 10, 12 and 14, and the board layout) and issue 151.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md` is new and owns the orchestrator record: files, fields, ids, stages, merge value, board and commands.
- `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`'s new "Report to an orchestrator" owns what a project lead writes when an orchestrator started it. `record-format.md` owns the new `run.orchestrator` field.
- `docs/design.md` §15.139 records the decisions.

### What changed, by file

- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/crew-orch.py` (new): the only writer of `<record-root>/orchestrators/<name>/`. Commands: `init`, `item add|pr|set`, `group add|order|owner`, `stage`, `doing`, `ask`, `inbox add`, `route`, `answer`, `dismiss`, `plan change`, `told`, `pace set`, `refresh`, `board [--urls]`, `show`. An `fcntl` lock and an atomic rename on every write. Python standard library only.
- `skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh` (new): the seeded test, 23 checks, with a temporary `CREW_RECORD_ROOT`, a stub `gh` and a stub `crew-usage.py`, run from outside the repo.
- `skills/orchestrator/references/orchestrator-record.md` (new): the canonical definition of the record.
- `skills/project-lead/scripts/crew-stats.py`: never walks into the top-level `orchestrators/` folder.
- `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md`: the section "Report to an orchestrator" (the `Orchestrator: <name>, item <id>` goal line, `run.orchestrator`, the stage calls per path, `ask` before each question), and a one-line pointer to it from "Take the goal".
- `skills/project-lead/references/record-format.md`: the `run.orchestrator` row and its writer/reader entry, and a pointer to the new reference.
- `skills/project-lead/references/autonomy-contract.md`, `skills/delivered-window/SKILL.md`: one pointer each to that section.
- `README.md` (The record), `CLAUDE.md` (layout, code list, authority list, build state), `docs/design.md` (§15.139).
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`: version `0.1.106`, assigned by the principal.

### Constraints that applied

- One writer, one canonical reference: Grep for `plan_changes`, `doing_at`, `stage_at`, `closed_at` over `skills/`, `agents/` and `hooks/` finds only the reference, the script and its test.
- Formats owned by sibling parts are not copied: the account-wide usage figures stay with issue 153 (`usage.json`, read through its `crew-usage.py` when present); the launcher's nine `launch` fields are the ones issue 152 prints.
- The plugin version (0.1.106) and the §15 number (139) were assigned by the principal.
- Public repo: no private names; the prior art in issue 149 was read for its faults only.
- `skills/project-lead/SKILL.md` is 555 lines against the 500-line target. It was 515 before; the new section is the one place that owns the project lead's reports.

### How this was verified

- `bash skills/orchestrator/scripts/test-crew-orch.sh` from `/private/tmp`: all 23 checks pass (AC1 to AC10, AC12, a new-process read-back, and the absent or failing `crew-usage.py`).
- A hand run of `board --urls` on a seeded record printed the #150 sections in order: Needs you, the group in merge order with its marks, Single items, Done, Links.
- `show` output keys compared with the reference's field tables: they match.
- A spec critic (two rounds' worth of findings applied) and a split critic (two rounds) reviewed the spec and the split before any code.

### Known gaps

- No orchestrator and no project lead has used this yet; the `crew:orchestrator` skill (issue 154) and the board pane (issue 155) are later parts.
- `crew-stats.py` fails under macOS's `/usr/bin/python3` 3.9 because `spend.py` already uses `str | None` at run time. This predates this change; `crew-orch.py` runs on 3.9.

triage.summary: Adds the orchestrator record and its sole writer, crew-orch.py. The script holds items, groups with merge order, an inbox, plan and told files. It reads PR state from gh, derives a merge value and prints a board. It comes with a seeded shell test and a reference spec. The change also tells project leads to report stages and questions to an orchestrator when the goal carries an Orchestrator: line, wires stage writes into the delivered-window and skeptical-review docs, makes crew-stats.py skip the orchestrators/ directory, and bumps the plugin version.

finding.claim: A ticket URL is stored with no scheme check and is later printed as a clickable OSC 8 link on a terminal.
finding.suggested_fix: Accept only http(s):// URLs in ticket_from/check_ticket, or in Links.make.
finding.explanation: A file: or other non-web scheme becomes a clickable terminal link, because only control characters are removed from it.

quotes: return {"id": opts["ticket"], "url": opts.get("ticket-url")}
or not isinstance(value.get("url"), (str, type(None)))):
first.rationale: The ticket URL is only checked to be a string. `Links.make` cleans control characters and then wraps the URL in OSC 8, so a `file:` or other scheme would become a link. The risk is small: the caller is the trusted orchestrator, escape injection is already stripped, and terminals decide whether to open non-web schemes.

quotes: return {"id": opts["ticket"], "url": opts.get("ticket-url")}
url = clean(url) if url else url
head.append(links.make(group["ticket"]["id"], group["ticket"].get("url")))
escalated.rationale: The claim is true. `ticket_from` and `check_ticket` accept any string as the URL, and `Links.make` only removes control characters before it wraps the URL in an OSC 8 link on a tty. The board shows group ticket URLs this way. But the URL comes from the local user's own command line or agent, and a person still has to click the link, so the security impact is very small.

finding.claim: When the first refresh of a PR item fails, the error is never stored, because the item has no github object yet.
finding.suggested_fix: When gh is None, store a minimal github object (or a separate field) that holds the error.

quotes: An item with a PR has no `github` until its first `refresh`
first.rationale: The code only stores the error when `github` already exists, so a first-time failure leaves `github` null and the error goes to stderr only. This fits the documented design (`github` stays null until a first successful refresh, and the failure is printed). The effect is small: a record reader can't tell a failed read from one that never ran.
